issues.legal_issue: A genuine land transfer made for adequate consideration in the ordinary management of the transferor’s affairs, with an irrevocable divestment of all interest and no indications of collusion or an intent to evade the ceiling law, need not be supported by proof of an impelling necessity to qualify for protection from being disregarded in a ceiling determination.
material_facts: The landholder sold two parcels by registered instruments to purchasers who were not alleged to be related to him.
The Appellate Authority found that the sales were genuine, but disregarded them because it considered that no compelling necessity for the sales had been shown.
The sales were for adequate consideration, were not benami, and reserved no immediate or deferred benefit for the landholder or his family.
The landholder transferred all interest in the land, including cultivatory possession, irrevocably, and made the sales in the ordinary management of his affairs to raise funds to build a residence.
There were no circumstances indicating collusion or an intention to defraud or circumvent the ceiling law.
issues.conclusion: The transfers qualified for protection under Section 5(6), Proviso (b), and could not be ignored merely because the landholder had not proved an impelling necessity; the ceiling authority had to take them into account.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5(6), Proviso (b), and Explanation II, as applied in Brijendra Singh v. State of U.P. (Civil Appeal No. 2726 of 1980, judgment dated November 25, 1980), a transferor discharges the onus of establishing good faith by showing that a transfer was made in the ordinary management of his affairs for adequate consideration and that he genuinely and irrevocably divested himself of all rights and possession, provided there are no circumstances suggesting collusion or an intention to defraud or circumvent the ceiling law. The transferor need not additionally prove an impelling need or pressing legal necessity.

rule.if: ceiling_surplus_determination and transfer_genuine and adequate_consideration and ordinary_management and irrevocable_divestment and no_collusion_or_evasion_indicia

predicates.ceiling_surplus_determination: A proceeding determines whether land held by a person is surplus under a landholding ceiling regime.
predicates.transfer_genuine: The landholder made a genuine transfer of the land to another person.
predicates.adequate_consideration: The transferee paid adequate consideration for the land.
predicates.ordinary_management: The landholder made the transfer in the ordinary management of his affairs.
predicates.irrevocable_divestment: The landholder genuinely and irrevocably gave up all rights and possession in the land, retaining no benefit for himself or his family.
predicates.no_collusion_or_evasion_indicia: The circumstances do not suggest collusion or an intent by the landholder to defraud or circumvent the ceiling regime.

issues.definition: When a ceiling determination concerns a genuine, adequately paid transfer made in ordinary management with irrevocable divestment and no indications of collusion or evasion, the transferred land must be counted as transferred rather than retained by the landholder.

issues.legal_issue: A ceiling authority making a fresh determination must use a land classification that was decided in the same proceedings and became final when upheld on appeal.
material_facts: The Appellate Authority held that all the land was unirrigated.
The High Court upheld that determination.

The classification was therefore res judicata, and the Supreme Court directed the Prescribed Authority on remand to calculate the ceiling and surplus areas on the basis that all the land held on the crucial date was unirrigated.
issues.conclusion: The Prescribed Authority had to determine the ceiling and surplus areas on the basis that all the land held on the crucial date was unirrigated.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied res judicata to the land classification already decided by the Appellate Authority and upheld by the High Court, requiring that classification to govern the fresh ceiling determination.

predicates.ceiling_area_determination: A proceeding requires an authority to determine a person's ceiling and surplus land area.
predicates.land_classification_decided_and_final: A land classification was decided in the proceedings and became final after being upheld on review.

issues.definition: When a ceiling-area determination follows a final decision classifying the land, that final classification must govern the fresh determination.
